rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords are restricted in how they may use an applicant's criminal record in rental decisions, including bans on certain inquiries, drug/alcohol testing requirements, and improper distribution of criminal record information.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers in connection with the rental, lease, or sublease of real property in New Jersey, with exceptions for certain serious offenses and sex offender registrants.
rules.exemptions: Exceptions exist for drug-related criminal activity involving methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted housing premises, lifetime sex offender registrants, and certain serious convictions (e.g., murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking).
rules.citation: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 et seq. (Fair Chance in Housing Act)
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not require an applicant
to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to
obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the applicant has a conviction for certain serious crimes (murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, etc.) or is a lifetime sex offender registrant, which remain excluded from protection

rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination - Source of Lawful Income Protection
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent to a tenant based solely on the tenant's source of lawful income, including Section 8 housing vouchers.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlord-tenant relationships in New Jersey, with exceptions for certain small owner-occupied dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for one sex as it pertains to familial status.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income.
